newCells.name: Abstract art
newCells.description: Painting and sculpture that does not describe a visible subject, built from form, colour, line and material alone. It became a stated programme in Europe around 1910, when Kandinsky, Malevich and Mondrian each argued that a picture holds together with no thing in it. The argument has been reopened in every generation since, under a new name each time.

maps.explanation: A direction in painting and sculpture, argued out in manifestos and exhibitions from about 1910.

questions: Impressionism, Cubism, Futurism and Surrealism sit above this cell in most histories, under a Modernism cell that does not exist here. Whether to make one is the owner's call.

newCells.name: Performance art
newCells.description: Work in which the artist is present and what they do is the material, made in front of an audience or recorded for one. It gathered as a named practice in the 1960s, and its terms are time, space, the body, the artist's presence, and the relation to the public. Usually only a photograph or a film is left afterwards, and how much of the work that carries is argued about inside the practice.

maps.explanation: A practice in the visual arts with its own literature, museums and canon since the 1960s.

questions: Fluxus, Gutai and Body Art are all made by doing something in front of people, and all three are left as roots or placed elsewhere; whether any of them sits under this cell needs a reading of their own sources.

newCells.name: Information design
newCells.description: Drawing made to explain something: a quantity, a network, an assembly, a route. The work is in choosing what to leave out, what to hold constant, and what the reader is meant to compare, so the drawing answers a question. Otto Neurath's pictorial statistics and Harry Beck's diagram of the London Underground are the cases it is taught from.

maps.explanation: A drawing practice with a canon and a taught method, holding the pictorial statistics and diagram cells.
Taught inside graphic design and applied to signage, timetables and instructions.

questions: Technical illustration is placed here because it draws to explain, though its home discipline is engineering documentation. The owner may prefer it as a root.

edges.explanation: A form of abstract art based on geometric elements, usually in non-illusionistic space.
Michel Tapié's label covers the abstract and gestural tendencies that developed in France and the rest of Europe during the war.
Van Doesburg, Herbin, Hélion and Vantongerloo started the association to keep abstract art going after painting had turned back to representation in the 1920s.
Korean criticism places the grouping inside its argument over how to write a history of abstract art there.
The synchromies were among the first abstract paintings made by American artists.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of abstract art, and both its gestural and its field manner drop the described subject.
Greenberg's term names abstract painting that had dropped the loaded gesture for flat colour, so it names a strand inside abstraction.
The movement rests on a strong emphasis on geometrical abstraction, in van Doesburg's formulation and in Max Bill's.
Malevich built it from circles, squares and rectangles in a limited palette, which is the geometric case of abstraction.
The group used only straight horizontal and vertical lines and rectangular forms, which is the route to abstraction its own account describes.
Its own article defines the term as a form of abstract art working through manipulated geometrical patterns.
The Brazilian group split off from the Concrete art movement, rejecting its rationalism while keeping its vocabulary.
Closely related to Abstract Expressionism, with many of the first proponents among the pioneering Abstract Expressionists.
The movement was built of Abstract Expressionist artists, with Morris Louis and Kenneth Noland at its head.
The painters trained in Abstract Expressionism and kept its handling when they returned to the figure, which is why the result is called a hybrid.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of Impressionism, and described as related to the European movement and practised in the United States.

The Post-Impressionism article lists Neo-Impressionism among what the term encompasses and names Seurat as one of its four principal artists. Neo-Impressionism's own article never calls itself post-Impressionist, so the claim is the umbrella's and not the movement's.
Its own article opens "Cloisonnism is a style of post-Impressionist painting with bold and flat forms separated by dark contours", so the containment is the cell's own claim about itself.
The account of Post-Impressionism names Les Nabis among the groups it covers.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of Neo-Impressionism, and it is the dotted handling at the centre of that movement.
The painters are described as part of an art movement advancing Realism, working inside the Romanticism then dominant.
American realism's own account treats the Ashcan painters as its core group in painting and Robert Henri as an American realist.
Its own article opens by calling it an American realist modern art movement.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of social realism, and social realism's own account treats the Mexican muralists as an important component of it.
Italian Renaissance painting divides into the Proto-Renaissance, the Early Renaissance, the High Renaissance and Mannerism.
A short period of exceptional production within the Italian Renaissance.
The Renaissance as it occurred north of the Alps.
Counted as the last of the four periods of Italian Renaissance painting, emerging out of the High Renaissance around 1520.
The Venetian school is treated as a major force in Italian Renaissance painting.
One of the canonical painting modes of the Renaissance, one of four available to Italian High Renaissance painters.
A style of medieval art, developed out of Romanesque art in twelfth-century northern France.
The illuminated bestiary is a medieval book form, and its pictures are among the most copied images of the period in northern Europe.
The final expression of the Baroque movement, also called Late Baroque.
Reynolds set the doctrine out in the Discourses he delivered at the Royal Academy, so it is the academies' idealising manner in portraiture.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of Romanticism, and the painters' vision is described as influenced by it.
The movements it covers came after Romanticism and took their material from it.
Recorded on Wikidata as a kind of Brazilian Romanticism, and it ran at the height of Romanticism in Brazil.
Recorded on Wikidata as part of the Hudson River School, whose second-generation painters worked in the manner.
An offshoot of Cubism, whose alternative name is Orphic Cubism.
Recorded on Wikidata as part of Cubism, and Ozenfant and Jeanneret set out their doctrine in an essay called After Cubism.
The work shares method or intent with earlier Dada, taken up again after the documentary publications of the 1950s.
Overtly inspired by the German Expressionist painters whose manner it revives.
Its own article opens by calling it the Italian version of Neo-Expressionism.
The account of Neo-Expressionism gives Junge Wilde as one of the names its painters were called.
A group of German Expressionist artists formed in Dresden in 1905. The cell already links to Expressionism, and this places it with the German Expressionist painting it made.
The work of the affiliated artists is assigned to German Expressionism.
Pincus-Witten coined the term for work influenced by Minimalism, or attempting to develop and go beyond it.
It emerged from the context of Conceptual art during the 1970s.
A group of conceptual artists running an exhibition space on the Lower East Side.
A happening is a performance, event or situation, usually as performance art.
Recorded on Wikidata as part of performance art, and placed among the 1960s efforts that developed performance, Fluxus, happening and body art.
A form of digital art drawn with graphical software, where the artist places each pixel.
The movement grew out of earlier internet art.
A subset of ukiyo-e, made by nearly every major print artist of the Edo period.
The movement revived ukiyo-e and kept its division of labour between artist, carver, printer and publisher.
Neurath and Arntz built the picture language to show social and economic facts under a fixed grammar, which is what this practice does.
The diagram drops geography to preserve the order of stops and the interchanges, so it is drawn around the rider's question.
The drawing is built so someone can assemble, service or understand the object, which is the explanatory purpose this practice is defined by.
A modernist art movement that emerged in the United States after the First World War.
Described as part of the larger genre of Latino futurisms.
Critics place the Bechers' approach in the lineage of the Neue Sachlichkeit movement of the 1920s, and their typologies are the model the class worked from.
